compiled_state.description:
Discovered while landing e9d5-c850-d505-4a5a (Gerrit change 2436). CI's
build-and-test / pytest job failed 3 consecutive times (all 3 python
versions each time) on the exact same test:

tests/unit/test_audit_serve_heldout.py::test_serve_binds_loopback_ephemeral_and_lists_ticket

Failure: RuntimeError: Network access is forbidden in unit/scripts tests...
raised despite the test carrying @pytest.mark.allow_network, which should
make tests/conftest.py's autouse _network_guard fixture skip patching
socket.socket.connect for this test.

Root-cause evidence gathered (not yet fully diagnosed):
- The test passes 100% reliably when run in isolation, or in small subsets,
  including with -n 4 --dist worksteal (5+ repeated local runs, 0 failures).
- The test only fails as part of a FULL-suite parallel run (pytest -m "not
  integration and not external and not repo_policy" -n 4 --dist worksteal
  against the whole tests/ tree) -- reproduced identically on 2 separate
  local full-suite runs, which is consistent with the CI failure signature.
- The same full-suite run also non-deterministically fails several OTHER,
  unrelated tests under load (test_atomic_completion_close.py,
  test_rebar_repo_isolation.py, test_tracker_footprint_cli.py) -- none of
  which share any code path with the audit-serve test or with e9d5's
  change, suggesting a general resource-contention/timing sensitivity
  across several tests when the full suite runs under xdist worksteal,
  not a defect specific to any one test or diff.
- This test spins up a REAL uvicorn server on a background thread and
  polls for readiness with a 10s deadline, then makes a REAL HTTP request
  to it -- exactly the kind of test that is sensitive to CPU/scheduler
  contention under a busy parallel test run.

Not fixed as part of e9d5 -- unrelated to that ticket's scope (typed
reconciler payload contracts), and per this repo's flaky-test policy a
flake must be root-caused rather than silently retried; this ticket is
the tracking vehicle for that root-cause.

Suggested follow-up:
- Confirm whether this and/or the other tests observed failing under load
  are known-flaky (check CI history across other recent changes for the
  same signature).
- If confirmed timing-sensitive under contention, consider widening the
  10s startup deadline model, isolating this test from -n xdist parallel
  scheduling (xdist_group), or another fix appropriate to its actual root
  cause once diagnosed.

Acceptance criteria:
- Root cause identified for why test_serve_binds_loopback_ephemeral_and_lists_ticket
  (and, if related, the other full-suite-only failures named above) fail
  under parallel/full-suite load but never in isolation.
- A fix applied (or a documented decision not to fix, e.g. an accepted
  ADR on test parallelism tradeoffs) and the affected test(s) demonstrated
  stable across N repeated full-suite CI runs.
compiled_state.title: Flaky test_serve_binds_loopback_ephemeral_and_lists_ticket under full-suite parallel load
